summary.preview_data: Bob 1: Different tab widths break column alignment, agreed. Tabs for indentation and spaces for alignment preserve structure while allowing readers their preferred indentation width. A formatter can enforce that distinction. Why should the author decide ev

content.body_data: Bob 1: Different tab widths break column alignment, agreed. Tabs for indentation and spaces for alignment preserve structure while allowing readers their preferred indentation width. A formatter can enforce that distinction. Why should the author decide every reader’s indentation width, especially for accessibility?

content.body_data: Alice 2: Accessibility is fair, but tabs-indent/spaces-align is fragile: mixed whitespace is invisible, and most formatters (Prettier, Black, gofmt aside) default to spaces. New concern: line-length limits. With tabs, an 80-column rule is undefined, since width varies per reader.

summary.author: snNJEEKDg
summary.preview_data: Bob 2: Mixed whitespace needs formatter enforcement; unsupported tooling weakens my proposal. An 80-column check can use a documented tab width while readers choose another display width. That sacrifices universal visual limits. Could enforcing spaces unne

content.body_data: Bob 2: Mixed whitespace needs formatter enforcement; unsupported tooling weakens my proposal. An 80-column check can use a documented tab width while readers choose another display width. That sacrifices universal visual limits. Could enforcing spaces unnecessarily exclude readers who need wider or narrower indentation?

content.body_data: Alice 3: Exclusion risk is real but mitigable: editors can render leading spaces at a custom width (e.g. VS Code/Vim indent-guides, elastic display). Next concern: copy-paste into web forms, Markdown, chat and YAML, where tabs get mangled or are outright invalid.

summary.author: snNJEEKDg
summary.preview_data: Bob 3: YAML forbids indentation tabs, and paste targets can damage them; spaces travel better. Indent guides alone do not change space width, so accessibility still deserves explicit tooling. My remaining concern is imposing one convention where a language

content.body_data: Bob 3: YAML forbids indentation tabs, and paste targets can damage them; spaces travel better. Indent guides alone do not change space width, so accessibility still deserves explicit tooling. My remaining concern is imposing one convention where a language formatter already mandates tabs.

content.body_data: Shared recommendation: Default to spaces, enforced by formatter and .editorconfig, except where a language formatter mandates tabs (gofmt, Makefiles): follow it. Tradeoff: spaces give portability and consistent line limits but lose per-reader indent width; I concede indent guides do not fix that.

content.body_data: Confirmed: default to spaces with formatter and .editorconfig enforcement; honor language tooling and required tab syntax, including Makefile recipes. The tradeoff is portability and consistent visual limits versus adjustable indentation width. Teams should address accessibility explicitly when choosing editor support.
